checks.correction: All confirmed in the releases, docs and collection_model_auth_options.go (OTP 180/8, auth 432000, file token 180, OTP max 86400, auth max about 3 years). Two details to add. The files docs describe the protected-file token as 'valid ~2min', while the code default is 180 s. Built-in backups are a ZIP of all of pb_data including local uploads, and the docs recommend sqlite3 .backup plus rsync once pb_data passes about 5 GB.

checks.claim: Node 24 moved to Maintenance LTS on 2026-10-20 (EOL 2028-04-30). Node 26 becomes Active LTS on 2026-10-28, and Node 22's EOL is 2027-04-30. node:sqlite is 'Stability 1.2 – Release candidate' since v24.15.0/v25.7.0. better-sqlite3 13.0.3 needs Node >= 22, and Fastify 5.12.7's LTS table lists Node 20 and 22.
checks.correction: Confirmed. The nodejs/release README still labels 24.x 'Active LTS' in its status column, but its dates put maintenance at 2026-10-20. Fastify's LTS table does not yet list Node 24 or 26, and Node 20 is already EOL, so the supported runtime for Fastify 5 is formally only Node 22.

checks.claim: Litestream v0.5.17 (2026-08-31) is current. v0.5.0 moved to LTX and cannot restore v0.3 WAL backups. v0.5 allows one replica per database, age encryption was removed, and R2 and B2 settings are auto-detected.
checks.correction: The 'cannot restore v0.3 backups' part is wrong for current releases. The migration guide says litestream restore 'restores from v0.3.x format backups without any special flags or configuration', added in v0.5.7. The rest holds: v0.5.17 is the latest, there is exactly one replica per database (more fails at startup), and 'Age encryption is not available in v0.5.0+' with no timeline for its return. That means the SQLite replica sits unencrypted in the bucket unless something else encrypts it. R2 (sign-payload, concurrency 2) and B2 (force-path-style) are auto-detected.

checks.claim: Email pricing: Resend Free is 3,000/month capped at 100/day, Pro $20 for 50k. Postmark Free is 100/month, Basic $15 for 10k at $1.80/1k extra. SES is $0.10/1k with a sandbox of 200/24 h and 1/s and a 96 h review. Cloudflare Email Sending (beta since 2026-04-16) needs Workers Paid, includes 3,000/month, then $0.35/1k, with free sends to verified destinations and binding, REST or SMTP.
checks.correction: All confirmed on the vendor pages. Resend Pro overage is $0.90 per 1k. SES gives an 'initial response within 96 hours'. Cloudflare's service page lists 'Workers binding, REST API, or authenticated SMTP'. Cloudflare Email Sending is still beta. Its free sends to verified destination addresses could cover a small, fixed family list, but each recipient must verify first.

checks.claim: A Home Screen web app has its own cookie and storage jar. Since 17.2 only cookies are copied in at install, and iOS 26 opens every Home Screen site as a web app with no manifest required. WebKit bug 272325 (open, P2) covers random session-cookie resets.
checks.correction: Confirmed. Safari 17.2: 'the cookies are copied over… No other kind of local storage is copied over.' Safari 26: 'By default, every website added to the Home Screen opens as a web app', and a manifest is no longer required. Bug 272325 is NEW, P2 with Critical severity, and last commented on 2024-11-21, including a 0.35% stale-cookie rate on iOS 18.1. The claim that no release documents Mail links opening inside the web app is an absence claim; I found nothing contradicting it. Out-of-scope links open in an in-app browser.

checks.claim: iOS web push needs 16.4+, a Home Screen web app and a permission request from a user gesture, with no Apple Developer account and *.push.apple.com allowed. Safari revokes subscriptions after silent pushes. Declarative Web Push ('web_push': 8030, title plus navigate, optional app_badge, window.pushManager) shipped in 18.4 with no silent-push penalty. iOS lacks pushsubscriptionchange, Background Sync and Background Fetch. Apple returns 403 BadJwtToken for a mailto:…@localhost subject.
checks.correction: All confirmed in the WebKit posts and MDN browser-compat-data: safari_ios has no pushsubscriptionchange (Chrome has it from 138), SyncManager and BackgroundFetchManager are unsupported in Safari, and Chrome has SyncManager from 49. web-push PR #988, adding the BadJwtToken note, merged on 2026-09-11. The Declarative Web Push post gives macOS 15.5 (Safari 18.5) as the desktop target.

checks.claim: The current Raspberry Pi OS images are dated 6 Oct 2026, on trixie with Linux 6.18. Chromium is 1:155.0.8059.79-1~deb13u1+rpt1 with an epoch, so Debian's chromium never replaces it. unattended-upgrades' default origins exclude the 'Raspberry Pi Foundation' archive.
checks.correction: The downloads page confirms 6 Oct 2026, kernel 6.18, Debian 13. The 6.18.50 point version comes only from Linuxiac. The Packages index confirms the chromium version; chromium-browser is a transitional package that depends on chromium. The Release file shows 'Origin: Raspberry Pi Foundation', and 50unattended-upgrades.Debian matches origin=Debian only. Also note that Debian trixie-security already has chromium 156.0.8078.47, so the Pi's Chromium is a major version behind upstream security and is not auto-updated.

checks.claim: Raspberry Pi's Touch Display 2 10" (announced 22 Jul 2026, $80, 1200×1920) needs 4-lane DSI and does not work with a Pi 4. The Waveshare 10.1" DSI LCD (C) works through the in-kernel 'vc4-kms-dsi-waveshare-panel,10_1_inch' overlay.
checks.correction: The Touch Display 2 part is right: OMG Ubuntu, Pimoroni and Waveshare all say it is not compatible with a Pi 4 or earlier. The announcement date is wrong: OMG Ubuntu dates the launch 23 July 2026. For the Waveshare (C), the overlay exists in the rpi-6.18.y README (with Goodix touch), and the wiki gives the trixie/bookworm line, brightness 0–255 through sysfs and 520 mA with the backlight on. But the wiki only ties the overlay's dual-DSI note to Pi 5/CM boards and describes the Pi 4B only through 15-pin FPC wiring, so verify that combination on a Pi 4 under trixie.

checks.claim: In Chromium, '--kiosk' skips the session-crashed bubble, the bad-flags warning and other startup infobars, and '--disable-infobars' no longer exists. AudioCaptureAllowedUrls grants mic access without a prompt ('*' not supported), AutoplayAllowlist allows autoplay, and both apply on Linux. From Chrome 136, remote debugging needs a non-default --user-data-dir.
checks.correction: Confirmed. infobar_utils.cc returns early under kiosk ('Do not show any other info bars in Kiosk mode') before both the crash bubble and ShowBadFlagsPrompt. The automation infobar is decided before that check, so it can still appear. chrome_switches.h has kiosk, no-first-run, start-maximized and hide-crash-restore-bubble, but no disable-infobars. The policy YAMLs show chrome.*:29- for AudioCaptureAllowedUrls with the explicit '*' exclusion, and chrome.*:86- for AutoplayAllowlist. Chrome's 2025-03-17 post confirms the Chrome 136 remote-debugging change.

checks.claim: raspi-config's overlay option installs overlayroot and prepends 'overlayroot=tmpfs' to cmdline.txt, so all changes outside /boot are lost at reboot. Making /boot read-only is a separate fstab option, and raspi-config refuses on 256 MB of RAM or less. cage 0.3.x lacks wlr-output-power-management, so wlopm fails, while labwc has it.
checks.correction: The trixie raspi-config confirms it: 'apt-get install -y overlayroot', 'sed … s/^/overlayroot=tmpfs /', a MemTotal <= 262144 check, and the read-only /boot handled through fstab. cage.c creates the output manager, screencopy, virtual keyboard, idle-notifier and idle-inhibit protocols but no output-power manager; labwc's server.c creates wlr_output_power_manager_v1. Under cage you can still blank through wlr-randr --off (output management) or the backlight's sysfs bl_power.

checks.claim: Cloudflare Zero Trust (Access) is free for up to 50 users, and pay-as-you-go is $7/user/month.
checks.correction: The 50-user free tier holds up: Cloudflare's 2020 post says '50 seats of Access and Gateway', and its pricing page describes the Free plan as for teams under 50 users. The current plans page I could load shows no per-seat price, so $7/user/month comes only from third-party summaries and is unverified. Every person (and the kiosk's identity) who logs in through Access takes a seat.

missing_considerations: PocketBase has no chunked or resumable upload, so any video over 100 MB cannot reach it through the tunnel in one multipart POST. Large videos need a tus sidecar with chunks under 100 MB, or browser-direct presigned multipart uploads to R2, with PocketBase only recording metadata. PocketBase's built-in backup ZIPs all of pb_data including media, which does not work at family-archive sizes; back up media and the DB separately.

Video playback makes repeated HTTP Range (206) requests over time. Safari will not play MP4 without Range support. Short-lived URL tokens (PocketBase file tokens of about 2–3 min, or short presigned GETs) can expire mid-playback and break seeking or resuming, so media auth needs a cookie or a token whose lifetime outlasts the longest video.

The iOS picker turns 4K HEVC into 4K H.264 .MOV, which is larger, and the Pi 4's H.264 decoder stops at 1080p. The server must therefore always make a ≤1080p, 8-bit SDR H.264/AAC MP4 with +faststart for the kiosk, and tone-map Dolby Vision/HLG HDR (zscale/libplacebo are in Debian's ffmpeg). Otherwise expect software decode at 150%+ CPU and washed-out colour. Also strip location metadata (-map_metadata -1) and EXIF GPS (sharp's default) on derivatives.

The two research tracks contradict each other on whether Pi Chromium uses V4L2 hardware decode on a Pi 4. trixie-feedback #101 settles it: it does. That makes Chromium rpt regressions in the V4L2 path a real kiosk risk, so pin a known-good Chromium build and test updates before rolling them out.

overlayroot=tmpfs wipes the Chromium profile at every reboot: the session cookie, service-worker cache, IndexedDB, the push subscription and storage.persist grants. Keep the profile on a writable partition (overlayroot=tmpfs:recurse=0 with /data), or design kiosk auth as a device credential that re-provisions itself at boot. Grandma cannot click a magic link.

The Pi has no RTC. If Chromium starts before NTP sync, TLS validation and cookie or token expiry checks can fail. Order the kiosk unit after time-sync.target (systemd-time-wait-sync enabled), and add a network-online wait and retry page.

Web Push in distro Chromium depends on Google's GCM/FCM and Google API keys. Unbranded Linux Chromium builds often cannot subscribe ('push service error'). Whether Raspberry Pi's Chromium can is unverified, so the kiosk should get live updates over SSE or WebSocket rather than Web Push.

Email link scanners that execute JavaScript (Defender Safe Links detonation) can auto-submit a landing page that consumes a token on load. iMessage and SMS link previews also fetch URLs. Make the token's consumption require a real user gesture or typed OTP entry. Because Mail opens links in Safari rather than the Home Screen app, a typed code inside the PWA is the reliable path on iOS.

If Cloudflare Access gates the whole hostname, the iOS standalone app and the kiosk must hold a CF_Authorization cookie too. When it expires, the Access login opens in an in-app browser, and the separate cookie jar can cause loops. Bot Fight Mode or challenges can also break service-worker and manifest fetches. Gating only admin paths with Access, or using the app's own auth, avoids this.

Uploads from iOS stop when the PWA is backgrounded or the screen locks (no Background Fetch or Background Sync). Large videos need tus resumability, visible progress and a 'keep this open' UX. The iOS 'Preparing…' transcode can also take minutes for long 4K clips before any byte is sent.

The kiosk's Chromium lags Debian security by a major version (155 vs 156) and is not covered by default unattended-upgrades. Lock it down with URLAllowlist/URLBlocklist, DeveloperToolsAvailability and IncognitoModeAvailability. getUserMedia and Wake Lock need a secure context, so the kiosk should load the https tunnel hostname, not plain LAN http, or the mic silently fails.

Litestream v0.5 has no encryption and allows a single replica. Family-photo metadata in R2 would sit unencrypted unless encrypted another way, and a second off-site copy needs storage-layer replication.

The trixie point release will bring libheif 1.23.4 and vips 8.16.1+deb13u2 (already in proposed-updates), and sharp's libvips floor rises with nearly every release. Pin the sharp version, or decode HEIC through libheif or the vips CLI outside sharp.
